title: A review report shows the findings it dismissed, and why
action:
Per D5 (store 7332c6ca). This lands in TWO places, and both are required — a report cannot display a bucket nothing was told to keep:

1. .bee/expertise/review.md, in or beside its `## Verify before reporting` section (:232-233, 'Reproduce or trace every suspected defect before you file it'). Today that section tells a reviewer to DROP what it cannot substantiate, and the drop leaves no trace. Add the keep-instruction: when a suspected defect is dropped, record it with the reason it was dropped. That record is what the report renders. Without this the display half is decorative.

2. skills/bee-reviewing/SKILL.md, beside the fixed summary line at :72 (`<N> finding(s) — P1 <a>, P2 <b>, P3 <c> · axis: spec <s>, standards <t>.`). The report gains a Dismissed section listing each dropped finding with its one-line reason. Say plainly why it exists: showing what the lead rejected lets a human override the judgement instead of trusting an invisible filter — the same honesty rule that already makes the zero-findings line verbatim at :75-76. Keep the existing summary line unchanged; the Dismissed section is additive, and a review that dismissed nothing shows no section rather than an empty one.

If skills/bee-reviewing/references/reviewing-reference.md carries the finding schema, add the dismissal's reason field there too so the schema and the report agree.

Run `bee dev regen` after touching skills/**.

acceptance: review.md instructs the reviewer to RECORD a dropped finding with its reason. bee-reviewing/SKILL.md describes the Dismissed section, additive to the unchanged summary line, absent when nothing was dismissed.
